name: Uruguay River flood, Uruguaiana-Itaqui (RS), Sep-Nov 2026

nisar.note: v0 polygons from a teammate render of the 010D Sep 30 -> Oct 12 pair; our own GCOV stack in progress

impacts.what: Itaqui: 29 people displaced by the Uruguay River
Uruguaiana: Uruguay River above flood stage

status: v0 — flood candidates from a teammate pair, to be reproduced; candidates, never confirmed
data_basis: NISAR GCOV (provisional + V1): our track 010 D stack Sep 18 → Nov 5 2026 (HH/HV frames + change maps; 0 gated flood candidates — the per-scene threshold sat at the −15 dB clamp on every pair) and track 082 D context frames; a teammate's NISAR Sep 30 → Oct 12 map (7 candidate polygons, 1.82 km²); upstream-basin rain forecast proof (IMERG Early + NOAA GFS, retrospective test). Local rain index (TPI) not replayed: local rain never reached its P99.

forecast_proof.question: Would the upstream-rain signal have warned Uruguaiana before the Oct 2026 Uruguay River flood?
forecast_proof.answer_short: Yes, 5 days before the river reached flood stage at Uruguaiana (Oct 5) and 8 days before the Itaqui displacement (Oct 8): satellite rain already observed over the upstream basin (IMERG Early) plus the NOAA GFS run of Sep 30 put the basin 3-day total above the season's 99th percentile. Second rise: 6 days before Oct 29 (>= p95, Oct 23). The GFS forecast alone did not flag either rise; local rain at Uruguaiana never reached its own 99th percentile.

signal.basin: Uruguay River upstream of the Uruguaiana gauge, HydroBASINS v1c lev07, 192,578 km2 (73-point 0.5 deg lattice)
signal.rain: basin-mean 3-day and 7-day totals ending D..D+6: observed IMERG Early (days < D) + NOAA GFS 00Z run of D (days >= D)
signal.climatology: NASA POWER IMERG Final daily 2001-2025, Sep-Nov; 3-day p95 62.5 / p99 100.3 mm; 7-day p95 119.5 / p99 152.1 mm

lead_time_days.gfs_forecast_only: no flag before either crossing (Sep 29 run: 50.7 mm 3-day vs p95 62.5; observed Sep 28-29: 93 mm)
lead_time_days.local_rain_at_uruguaiana: 72 h rain never >= local 3-day P99 (max 0.85x, Oct 6) -> a local-rain index would not have warned

false_alarms.p95_strict_median_basis: Sep 18 + Nov 1-6 (Nov 1-6 precede the Nov 12-13 red alert at 8.46-8.52 m)

where.method: river corridor HAND <= 5 m (90 m HAND) inside the AOI vs the radar new-water candidate polygons at Uruguaiana (7 polygons, 1.85 km2, about 29 people)
where.reading: the signal points to the river corridor, not to specific neighbourhoods: the floodplain is flat (lift 1.5)

caveats: IMERG Final is not out for Sep-Nov 2026: observed rain is IMERG Early (Early ran 1.34x Final on RS 2024 Apr 27). Scaling Early by 1/1.34: Sep 30 basin 3-day 75.7 mm (< p99 100.3, >= p95 62.5) -> still 5 d before Oct 5 at p95; second rise first flag moves from Oct 23 to Oct 24 -> 5 d before Oct 29.
Flood-candidate polygons are candidates, never confirmed; 082D NISAR pairs are dominated by rice-paddy flooding and are not used here.

SGB publishes hours-ahead level forecasts (e.g. 9.91 m for 23:00 on Oct 13) and Defesa Civil RS issued alerts (cota de alerta Oct 28); no public alert dated before Oct 5 was found -> no claim of being earlier than official warnings.
'Would have given N days notice', never 'prevented'.

tpi_replay_note: Local rain index not replayed for this case; local rain at Uruguaiana never reached its own P99 — the flood was driven by upstream-basin rain (see forecast_proof).
